note: Reviewed CDB90 match 154, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The 6 August 1824 engagement was between the opposing cavalry components, ahead of the larger infantry armies. The Spanish Army historical account describes about 900 Patriot and 1300 Royalist cavalry, which are the lower endpoints of the CDB estimates, rather than the entire 10000/8000-person campaign armies. Preserve the CDB 2000/2000 estimates and their signed uncertainty; the local display names clarify cavalry scope without narrowing the counts to one named regiment. Santa Cruz’s report identifies the participating cavalry commands. No infantry equipment profile is inferred. These sources review event and force identity; CDB numerical estimates and uncertainty are retained, not independently certified. The agreement with the lower endpoints does not independently confirm either 2000 central estimate or equal opposing strengths: Santa Cruz describes the Patriot cavalry as numerically inferior. The figures remain competing estimates for the cavalry engagement, not a reconstructed count of the larger infantry armies. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name PATRIOT ARMY): Santa Cruz’s report identifies the cavalry engagement, with the Patriot cavalry numerically inferior. The Spanish Army account estimates 900 Patriot and 1300 Royalist cavalry; these are within the CDB ranges. The original CDB 2000/2000 central estimates remain unchanged and do not establish equal historical strengths. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name SP ARMY): Santa Cruz’s report identifies the cavalry engagement, with the Patriot cavalry numerically inferior. The Spanish Army account estimates 900 Patriot and 1300 Royalist cavalry; these are within the CDB ranges. The original CDB 2000/2000 central estimates remain unchanged and do not establish equal historical strengths.
